scope: Source-verified rule map: NY Medicaid + Anthem NY; federal Medicare (incl. Medicare Advantage, NCD/LCD), Medicaid enrollment and ERISA; California and Florida overpayment statutes; UnitedHealthcare, Fidelis/Centene and EmblemHealth policies

rules.title: NY Medicaid managed-care provider enrollment requirement
rules.authority: New York State Department of Health
rules.currentSourceStatement: NYSDOH states that providers joining a managed care network also have to enroll with the New York State Medicaid program.

citation.sourceTitle: NYSDOH — Information for Health Care Providers
citation.excerpt: Providers will also have to enroll with the New York State Medicaid program.

rules.title: Anthem NY billed-code documentation support
rules.authority: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New York
rules.currentSourceStatement: Anthem states that billed CPT, HCPCS and/or revenue codes should be fully supported in the medical record or office notes.

citation.sourceTitle: Anthem NY — Reimbursement policies
citation.excerpt: The billed code(s) should be fully supported in the medical record and/or office notes.

pdfCitation.locator: PDF viewer p. 171; manual printed p. 170 — Reimbursement Policies
pdfCitation.excerpt: The billed code(s) are required to be fully supported in the medical record and/or office notes.

rules.title: Anthem NY reimbursement-policy precedence
rules.authority: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New York
rules.currentSourceStatement: Anthem states that its reimbursement policies may be superseded by state, federal or CMS requirements.

citation.sourceTitle: Anthem NY — Reimbursement policies
citation.excerpt: These policies may be superseded by state, federal or CMS requirements.

pdfCitation.locator: PDF viewer p. 171; manual printed p. 170 — Reimbursement Hierarchy
pdfCitation.excerpt: These policies may be superseded by mandates in provider, state, federal or CMS contracts.

rules.title: CMS Medicaid NCCI Policy Manual — 2026
rules.currentSourceStatement: CMS states that the 2026 Medicaid NCCI Policy Manual is effective January 1, 2026 and that prior annual versions are archived.

citation.sourceTitle: CMS — Medicaid NCCI Policy Manual
citation.excerpt: CMS updates the NCCI Policy Manual for Medicaid Services once a year.

rules.title: Anthem NY provider claim-payment dispute path
rules.authority: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New York
rules.currentSourceStatement: Anthem provides a provider payment dispute process for finalized claims when a provider disagrees with the outcome.

citation.sourceTitle: Anthem NY — Claims submissions and disputes
citation.excerpt: Provider payment disputes apply when a provider disagrees with a finalized claim outcome.

rules.title: Medicare payment requires sufficient information
rules.currentSourceStatement: Federal regulation lists furnishing sufficient information to determine whether payment is due as a condition of Medicare payment.

citation.excerpt: must furnish to the intermediary or carrier sufficient information to determine whether payment is due and the amount of payment

rules.title: Medicare covers only reasonable and necessary services
rules.currentSourceStatement: The Social Security Act excludes from Medicare payment items and services that are not reasonable and necessary for diagnosis or treatment, subject to the statute’s stated exceptions.

citation.sourceTitle: 42 U.S.C. § 1395y (Social Security Act § 1862)
citation.excerpt: are not reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of illness or injury or to improve the functioning of a malformed body member

rules.title: Outpatient therapy requires a written plan of treatment
rules.currentSourceStatement: Outpatient rehabilitation services must be furnished under a written plan of treatment.

citation.excerpt: must be furnished under a written plan of treatment

rules.title: Therapy plan is established before treatment begins
rules.currentSourceStatement: The plan of treatment is established before treatment begins by a physician, the treating therapist, or another listed practitioner.

citation.excerpt: The plan is established before treatment is begun by one of the following

rules.title: Therapy plan content
rules.currentSourceStatement: The plan states the type, amount, frequency and duration of services, and indicates the diagnosis and anticipated goals.

citation.excerpt: prescribes the type, amount, frequency, and duration of the physical therapy, occupational therapy, or speech-language pathology services to be furnished to the individual, and indicates the diagnosis and anticipated goals

rules.title: Therapy plan changes must be written and signed
rules.currentSourceStatement: Changes to the plan must be made in writing and signed by a listed practitioner.

citation.excerpt: Are made in writing and signed by one of the following

rules.title: Therapy plan: signature, professional identity and date
rules.currentSourceStatement: The Medicare Benefit Policy Manual states that the signature, professional identity and date of the person who established the therapy plan must be recorded with the plan.

citation.sourceTitle: Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15
citation.excerpt: The signature and professional identity (e.g., MD, OTR/L) of the person who established the plan, and the date it was established must be recorded with the plan.

rules.title: Therapy plan certification requires a dated signature
rules.currentSourceStatement: Certification of the therapy plan of care requires a dated signature on the plan or another document indicating approval.

citation.sourceTitle: Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15
citation.excerpt: Certification requires a dated signature on the plan of care or some other document that indicates approval of the plan of care.

rules.title: Timed-code unit table (8-minute rule)
rules.currentSourceStatement: The Claims Processing Manual converts total timed-code minutes to billable units; 8 through 22 minutes is one unit.

citation.sourceTitle: Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 5
citation.excerpt: 1 unit: 8 minutes through 22 minutes

rules.title: Retrospective billing before the enrollment effective date
rules.currentSourceStatement: Physical therapists, occupational therapists and speech-language pathologists, among others, may retrospectively bill up to 30 days before the effective date if circumstances precluded enrollment in advance.

citation.excerpt: may retrospectively bill for services when the provider or supplier has met all program requirements

rules.title: Home health face-to-face encounter timing
rules.currentSourceStatement: Home health certification requires a face-to-face encounter within 90 days before or 30 days after the start of care.

citation.excerpt: occurred no more than 90 days prior to the home health start of care date or within 30 days of the start of the home health care

rules.title: Hospice certification before claim submission
rules.currentSourceStatement: Subject to stated exceptions, the hospice must obtain the written certification of terminal illness before submitting a claim.

citation.excerpt: the hospice must obtain the written certification before it submits a claim for payment

rules.title: Hospice certification prognosis statement
rules.currentSourceStatement: The certification must specify a prognosis of a life expectancy of 6 months or less if the terminal illness runs its normal course.

citation.excerpt: prognosis is for a life expectancy of 6 months or less if the terminal illness runs its normal course

rules.title: Hospice clinical information supporting prognosis
rules.currentSourceStatement: Clinical information supporting the prognosis must accompany the certification and be filed in the medical record.

citation.excerpt: Clinical information and other documentation that support the medical prognosis must accompany the certification

rules.title: Hospice certification for each benefit period
rules.currentSourceStatement: The Medicare Benefit Policy Manual repeats that written certification is required for each benefit period.

citation.sourceTitle: Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 9
citation.excerpt: The hospice must obtain written certification of terminal illness for each benefit period, even if a single election continues in effect.

rules.title: Medical review signature requirements
rules.currentSourceStatement: Contractors consider the totality of the medical record when reviewing whether the person responsible for care is identifiable; signatures are required to satisfy specific rules or to resolve authenticity concerns.

citation.sourceTitle: Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 3
citation.excerpt: Medicare contractors shall consider the totality of the medical record when reviewing for compliance with the above.

rules.title: Supplier proof of delivery retention
rules.currentSourceStatement: Suppliers must keep proof of delivery documentation for seven years from the date of service.

citation.sourceTitle: Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 4
citation.excerpt: Proof of delivery documentation must be maintained in the supplier's files for seven years

rules.title: Extrapolation limited to sustained error or failed education
rules.currentSourceStatement: Medicare contractors may not use extrapolation to determine overpayments unless there is a sustained or high level of payment error, or documented educational intervention has failed.

citation.sourceTitle: 42 U.S.C. § 1395ddd (Social Security Act § 1893)
citation.excerpt: may not use extrapolation to determine overpayment amounts to be recovered by recoupment, offset, or otherwise unless the Secretary determines that

rules.title: Statistical sampling and extrapolation instructions
rules.currentSourceStatement: The Program Integrity Manual gives contractors instructions on statistical sampling and estimating overpayments.

citation.sourceTitle: Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 8
citation.excerpt: The purpose of this section is to provide instructions for contractors on the use of statistical sampling in their reviews and estimation of overpayments

rules.title: Recoupment limited while a reconsideration is pending
rules.currentSourceStatement: For a provider or supplier that seeks a qualified independent contractor reconsideration, recoupment may not begin until the reconsideration decision is rendered.

citation.sourceTitle: 42 U.S.C. § 1395ddd (Social Security Act § 1893)
citation.excerpt: the Secretary may not take any action (or authorize any other person, including any medicare contractor, as defined in subparagraph (C)) to recoup the overpayment until the date the decision on the reconsideration has been rendered

rules.title: Redetermination request deadline
rules.currentSourceStatement: A redetermination request must be filed within 120 calendar days of receiving the notice of the initial determination, subject to the good-cause exception.

citation.excerpt: any request for redetermination must be filed within 120 calendar days from the date a party receives the notice of the initial determination

rules.title: Reconsideration request deadline
rules.currentSourceStatement: A QIC reconsideration request must be filed within 180 calendar days of receiving the redetermination notice.

citation.excerpt: any request for a reconsideration must be filed within 180 calendar days from the date the party receives the notice of the redetermination

rules.title: Contractor reopening within one year for any reason
rules.currentSourceStatement: A contractor may reopen on its own motion within one year of the initial determination or redetermination for any reason; longer periods apply for good cause and fraud.

citation.excerpt: Within 1 year from the date of the initial determination or redetermination for any reason

rules.title: When an overpayment is identified
rules.currentSourceStatement: A person has identified an overpayment when the person knowingly receives or retains it.

citation.excerpt: A person has identified an overpayment when the person knowingly receives or retains an overpayment

rules.title: Report and return deadline: 60 days
rules.currentSourceStatement: A person who has received an overpayment must report and return it by the later of 60 days after identification or the date any corresponding cost report is due.

citation.excerpt: The date which is 60 days after the date on which the overpayment was identified

rules.title: Overpayment lookback period: 6 years
rules.currentSourceStatement: An overpayment must be reported and returned if identified within 6 years of the date it was received.

citation.excerpt: within 6 years of the date the overpayment was received

rules.title: Medicaid ordering and referring providers must be enrolled
rules.currentSourceStatement: State Medicaid agencies must require ordering or referring professionals to be enrolled as participating providers.

citation.excerpt: must require all ordering or referring physicians or other professionals providing services under the State plan or under a waiver of the plan to be enrolled as participating providers

rules.title: Group health plan: at least 180 days to appeal an adverse determination
rules.currentSourceStatement: ERISA group health plan claims procedures must give claimants at least 180 days after an adverse benefit determination to appeal.

citation.excerpt: Provide claimants at least 180 days following receipt of a notification of an adverse benefit determination within which to appeal the determination

rules.title: Group health plan: medical-judgment appeals reviewed by a health care professional
rules.currentSourceStatement: When an appeal turns on a medical judgment, including whether treatment is not medically necessary, the plan fiduciary must consult an appropriately trained health care professional.

citation.excerpt: the appropriate named fiduciary shall consult with a health care professional who has appropriate training and experience in the field of medicine involved in the medical judgment

rules.title: Hospice aggregate cap
rules.currentSourceStatement: The hospice aggregate cap is the adjusted cap amount multiplied by the number of Medicare beneficiaries, by one of two stated methodologies. It is a provider-level calculation, not a claim finding.

citation.excerpt: A hospice's aggregate cap is calculated by multiplying the adjusted cap amount

rules.title: Medicare Advantage plans apply Traditional Medicare coverage conditions
rules.currentSourceStatement: Medicare Advantage organizations must comply with national coverage determinations and with general coverage and benefit conditions in Traditional Medicare law, unless superseded by MA-specific law.

citation.excerpt: General coverage and benefit conditions included in Traditional Medicare laws, unless superseded by laws applicable to MA plans

rules.title: Medicare Advantage reconsideration request deadline
rules.currentSourceStatement: A request for a standard reconsideration of an MA organization determination must be filed within 60 calendar days of receiving the written notice, subject to the good-cause provisions.

citation.excerpt: a request for reconsideration must be filed within 60 calendar days after receipt of the written organization determination notice

rules.title: National coverage determinations bind appeal adjudicators
rules.currentSourceStatement: An NCD is binding on contractors, QICs, ALJs and the Council.

citation.excerpt: An NCD is binding on fiscal intermediaries, carriers, QIOs, QICs, ALJs and attorney adjudicators, and the Council

rules.title: Local coverage determinations: substantial deference, not binding on ALJs
rules.currentSourceStatement: ALJs and the Council are not bound by LCDs or CMS program guidance but give them substantial deference when applicable.

citation.excerpt: are not bound by LCDs, LMRPs, or CMS program guidance, such as program memoranda and manual instructions, but will give substantial deference to these policies if they are applicable to a particular case

rules.title: California insurers: overpayment reimbursement request within 365 days
rules.currentSourceStatement: A California health insurer may not request reimbursement of an overpayment unless a written request is sent to the provider within 365 days of payment. A fraud-or-misrepresentation exception applies.

citation.sourceTitle: California Insurance Code § 10133.66 (California.Public.Law copy of the code)
citation.excerpt: unless a written request for reimbursement is sent to the provider within 365 days of the date of payment on the overpaid claim

rules.title: California plans: provider repays or contests an overpayment within 30 working days
rules.currentSourceStatement: After a plan’s notice of overpayment, the provider must reimburse within 30 working days or contest in writing within the same period.

citation.sourceTitle: California Health and Safety Code § 1371.1 (California.Public.Law copy of the code)
citation.excerpt: the provider shall reimburse the health care service plan within 30 working days of receipt by the provider of the notice of overpayment

rules.title: Florida insurers: overpayment claims within 30 months
rules.currentSourceStatement: For retroactive review or audit not related to fraud, a Florida health insurer must submit overpayment claims within 30 months of its payment.

citation.sourceTitle: Florida Statutes § 627.6131
citation.excerpt: All claims for overpayment must be submitted to a provider within 30 months after the health insurer's payment of the claim

rules.title: Florida insurers: overpayment claims within 12 months for listed licensed professionals
rules.currentSourceStatement: For providers licensed under chapters 458 (physicians), 459 (osteopaths), 460 (chiropractors), 461 (podiatrists), 466 (dentists) and 490 (psychologists), overpayment claims must be submitted within 12 months, except for providers convicted of fraud.

citation.sourceTitle: Florida Statutes § 627.6131
citation.excerpt: all claims for overpayment submitted to a provider licensed under chapter 458, chapter 459, chapter 460, chapter 461, chapter 466, or chapter 490 must be submitted to the provider within 12 months after the health insurer's payment of the claim

rules.title: Florida: provider must pay, deny or contest an overpayment claim within 40 days
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Florida provider must pay, deny or contest an insurer’s overpayment claim within 40 days of receipt; failure to pay or deny within 140 days creates an uncontestable obligation.

citation.sourceTitle: Florida Statutes § 627.6131
citation.excerpt: A provider must pay, deny, or contest the health insurer's claim for overpayment within 40 days after the receipt of the claim

rules.title: UnitedHealthcare Commercial: 8-minute minimum for one timed unit
rules.currentSourceStatement: UnitedHealthcare aligns with CMS: at least eight minutes of therapy are required to bill one 15-minute unit.

citation.sourceTitle: UnitedHealthcare Commercial — Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation: Maximum Combined Frequency per Day Policy (2026R0101A)
citation.excerpt: at least eight minutes of therapy services must be performed to meet the minimum time qualification to bill one 15 minute unit

rules.title: UnitedHealthcare Commercial: maximum four timed codes per date of service
rules.currentSourceStatement: UnitedHealthcare reimburses timed therapy codes in any combination up to four timed codes per date of service for the same specialty provider, subject to the policy’s exceptions.

citation.sourceTitle: UnitedHealthcare Commercial — Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation: Maximum Combined Frequency per Day Policy (2026R0101A)
citation.excerpt: up to a maximum of four timed codes (equivalent to one hour of therapy) per date of service

rules.title: UnitedHealthcare Commercial: assistants are not reimbursed for therapy evaluation codes
rules.currentSourceStatement: Therapy assistants are not reimbursed for PT or OT evaluation and re-evaluation codes.

citation.sourceTitle: UnitedHealthcare Commercial — Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation: PT, OT and Evaluation & Management Policy (2026R0098A)
citation.excerpt: Physical and Occupational Therapy Assistants will not be reimbursed for CPT codes 97161-97164 or 97165-97168

rules.title: UnitedHealthcare Commercial: CQ and CO modifiers for assistant services
rules.currentSourceStatement: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2020, services furnished in whole or in part by a PTA or OTA require modifier CQ or CO alongside GP or GO.

citation.sourceTitle: UnitedHealthcare Commercial — Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation: PT, OT and Evaluation & Management Policy (2026R0098A)
citation.excerpt: the HCPCS modifiers CQ and CO modifiers are required to be used for services furnished In Whole or In Part by a Physical Therapy Assistant (PTA) or Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA)

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: unsupported billed units may be denied or recouped
rules.currentSourceStatement: The Centene ABA documentation policy states that billed units not fully supported by documentation may be denied or recouped.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: Billed units not fully supported by documentation may be subject to payment denial or recoupment

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: prior authorization where required
rules.currentSourceStatement: ABA documentation must show prior authorization was obtained where required.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: Prior authorization approval for ABA services has been obtained, if required

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: required signatures and printed names
rules.currentSourceStatement: Clinical documentation must include the signature and printed names of the member or guardian, rendering clinician or technician and supervising practitioner, as applicable.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: signature and printed names of the member/enrollee, legal guardian, rendering clinician/technician and supervising practitioner

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: active treatment throughout billed time
rules.currentSourceStatement: Documentation must support that active treatment was delivered throughout the billed duration.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: Continuous and efficient use of session time that is clinically justified and consistent with treatment plan goals

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: service notes completed before claim submission
rules.currentSourceStatement: Service activity notes must be completed before the claim is submitted.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: Service activity notes for all services rendered are completed prior to claim submission

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: exact session date and start and end times
rules.currentSourceStatement: Notes must record the exact date and time of each session, including start and end time.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: Exact date and time of session to include start and end time

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: late-note creation date and rationale
rules.currentSourceStatement: If a note was created on a different date from the service, it must state the creation date and the reason.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: the note includes the date of note creation with rationale for why note was created on a date different than the service was rendered

rules.title: Fidelis/Centene ABA: protocol modification hours (97155/97158)
rules.currentSourceStatement: For 97155 and/or 97158, protocol modification must meet the stated hours threshold; the policy describes denial or recoupment of unsupported hours.

citation.sourceTitle: Fidelis Care / Centene — Clinical Policy CP.BH.105 ABA Documentation Requirements
citation.excerpt: Protocol modification occurs for at least two hours per week or 10% of the direct service hours provided, whichever is greater

rules.title: EmblemHealth Commercial: modifier 96 or 97 on habilitative and rehabilitative services
rules.currentSourceStatement: Effective 1/1/2025, claims for habilitative services require modifier 96 and rehabilitative services modifier 97; lines billed without the correct modifier are denied.

citation.sourceTitle: EmblemHealth — Billing for Habilitative and Rehabilitative Services Policy (Commercial), RPC20240052
citation.excerpt: EmblemHealth requires claims for habilitative and rehabilitative services to be billed according to the following guidelines

rules.title: EmblemHealth Commercial: denial when modifier 96 or 97 is missing
rules.currentSourceStatement: A claim line is denied if modifier 96 or 97 is missing on a habilitative or rehabilitative service.

citation.sourceTitle: EmblemHealth — Billing for Habilitative and Rehabilitative Services Policy (Commercial), RPC20240052
citation.excerpt: Denied if modifier 96 or 97 is not billed on a habilitative or rehabilitative service

rules.title: Arizona health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: Except in cases of fraud, an Arizona insurer or provider may not adjust or request adjustment of a paid or denied claim more than one year after payment or denial.

citation.sourceTitle: Arizona Revised Statutes § 20-3102
citation.excerpt: shall not adjust or request adjustment of the payment or denial of a claim more than one year after the health care insurer has paid or denied that claim

rules.title: Connecticut health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A contracting health organization may not cancel, deny or demand return of payment for an authorized covered service because of administrative or eligibility error more than eighteen months after receipt of a clean claim, subject to stated exceptions.

citation.sourceTitle: Connecticut General Statutes § 38a-479b (chapter 700c)
citation.excerpt: more than eighteen months after the date of the receipt of a clean claim

rules.title: Delaware health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Delaware health insurer or plan may not initiate overpayment recovery efforts more than 12 months after the original payment; recovery is initiated when the insurer first identifies the error through an initial audit report or similar communication.

citation.sourceTitle: 18 Delaware Code § 2730
citation.excerpt: may not initiate overpayment recovery efforts more than 12 months after the original payment for the claim was made

rules.title: Kansas health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Kansas insurer may not initiate a reimbursement request or otherwise seek to recoup an erroneous payment unless initiated within 18 months after the end of the month of payment.

citation.sourceTitle: Kansas Statutes § 40-2442
citation.excerpt: unless such action is initiated within 18 months after the end of the month in which the erroneous payment was made

rules.title: Maryland health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (6 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Maryland carrier may retroactively deny reimbursement only during the 6-month period after payment (18 months where coordination of benefits with another carrier, Medicaid or Medicare applies).

citation.sourceTitle: Maryland Insurance Code § 15-1008
citation.excerpt: during the 6-month period after the date that the carrier paid the health care provider

rules.title: Missouri health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Missouri health carrier may not request a refund or offset against a claim more than twelve months after payment, except for fraud or misrepresentation by the provider.

citation.sourceTitle: Missouri Revised Statutes § 376.384
citation.excerpt: more than twelve months after a health carrier has paid a claim

rules.title: South Carolina health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A South Carolina insurer may not initiate overpayment recovery more than eighteen months after the initial payment was received by the provider.

citation.sourceTitle: South Carolina Code § 38-59-250
citation.excerpt: more than eighteen months after the initial payment was received by the provider

rules.title: Texas health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (180 days)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Texas insurer may recover an overpayment from a physician or provider only if, by the 180th day after the provider received the payment, it gives written notice stating the basis and specific reasons for the request. The anchor is the date the provider received the payment and the milestone is written notice of the overpayment.

citation.sourceTitle: Texas Insurance Code § 1301.132 (texas.public.law copy of the code)
citation.excerpt: not later than the 180th day after the date the physician or provider receives the payment

rules.title: Virginia health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Virginia carrier may not impose a retroactive denial or seek recovery of a paid claim unless the claim was fraudulent, the provider was already paid or did not deliver the service, or no more than 12 months have elapsed; 30 days’ written notice is required.

citation.sourceTitle: Code of Virginia § 38.2-3407.15
citation.excerpt: the time which has elapsed since the date of the payment of the original challenged claim does not exceed 12 months

rules.title: Washington health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (24 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: Except for fraud, a Washington carrier may not request a refund of a payment unless it does so in writing within twenty-four months of payment (six months for mental health and substance use disorder services, per the statute).

citation.excerpt: within twenty-four months after the date that the payment was made

rules.title: West Virginia health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A West Virginia health plan may retroactively deny a claim only for the reasons listed in the statute for one year from the original payment; two categories have no time limit.

citation.sourceTitle: West Virginia Code § 33-45-2
citation.excerpt: for a period of one year from the date the claim was originally paid

rules.title: Alabama health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: An Alabama insurer may not retroactively deny, adjust or seek recoupment of a paid claim after one year from the initial payment, other than for fraud, coordination of benefits or duplicate payments.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes Ala. Code § 27-1-17; the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: after the expiration of one year from the date that the initial claim was paid

rules.title: Alaska health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (365 days)
rules.currentSourceStatement: An Alaska health care insurer may not initiate recovery of an overpayment more than 365 days after the original payment unless it has clear and documented reason to believe the provider committed fraud or other intentional misconduct.

citation.sourceTitle: 3 AAC 26.110(d) (Alaska Administrative Code, Justia regulations copy, current through May 30, 2025)
citation.excerpt: more than 365 days after the date the original payment was made

rules.title: Arkansas health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: Except for fraud by the provider, an Arkansas insurer may recoup from a provider only during the eighteen months after it paid the claim.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes Ark. Code § 23-63-1803; the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: only during the eighteen-month period after the date that the healthcare insurer paid the claim

rules.title: Colorado health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: Where there is no contract between provider and carrier, Colorado claim adjustments must be made within twelve months after the original explanation of benefits, for both provider and carrier.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes C.R.S. § 10-16-704(4.5); the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: within twelve months after the date of the original explanation of benefits

rules.title: Georgia health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Georgia audit or retroactive denial of payment must be completed, with notice, within the sooner of 18 months after the initial claim submission or 24 months after the date of service.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes O.C.G.A. § 33-20A-62; the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: within the sooner of 18 months after the claimant's initial submission

rules.title: Hawaii health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Hawaii entity may not initiate recoupment or offset more than eighteen months after the initial payment (seventy-two months for fraud or material misrepresentation); self-insured groups and federal programs are excluded.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes Haw. Rev. Stat. § 431:13-108; the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: more than eighteen months after the initial claim payment was received by the health care provider or health care entity

rules.title: Indiana health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (24 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: An Indiana insurer may not, more than two years after an overpayment was made, request repayment or adjust a later claim to recover it.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes Ind. Code § 27-8-5.7-10; the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: more than two (2) years after the date on which an overpayment on a provider claim was made

rules.title: Kentucky health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (24 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: Except for fraud, a Kentucky insurer may retroactively deny reimbursement to a provider only during the twenty-four months after paying the claim.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes KRS § 304.17A-708; the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: twenty-four (24) month period after the date that the insurer paid the claim

rules.title: Louisiana health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A Louisiana health insurance issuer may not retroactively deny, adjust or seek recoupment of a paid claim after eighteen months from the initial payment.

citation.sourceTitle: La. R.S. 22:1838 (2025 Louisiana Laws, Justia copy of the code)
citation.excerpt: after the expiration of eighteen months from the date the initial claim was paid

rules.title: Montana health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: Where the issuer does not limit the provider’s claim-submission time, a Montana issuer may not request reimbursement or offset for an invalid or overpaid claim more than 12 months after payment, subject to stated exceptions.

citation.sourceTitle: SECONDARY SOURCE — 50-State Survey: Look Back Laws (quotes Mont. Code Ann. § 33-22-150; the statute text has not yet been checked)
citation.excerpt: more than 12 months after the payment of an invalid or overpaid claim

rules.title: New Hampshire health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (12 months)
rules.currentSourceStatement: A New Hampshire carrier may not impose a retroactive denial of a previously paid claim unless it gave the reason in writing and no more than 12 months have elapsed since payment.

citation.sourceTitle: N.H. RSA 420-J:8-b (2025 New Hampshire Revised Statutes, Justia copy of the code)
citation.excerpt: does not exceed 12 months

rules.title: New Jersey health insurers: overpayment recovery limit (18 months)

citation.excerpt: The Provider must make a direct reimbursement to the Authority within thirty (30) calendar days from the date of the notice of the Overpayment

rules.title: Oregon Medicaid: an appeal does not change the repayment due date
rules.currentSourceStatement: Asking for a hearing or administrative review does not move the repayment date. If the appeal reduces the amount, the Authority handles the amount already paid as the rule provides.

citation.sourceTitle: OAR 410-120-1397 Recovery of Overpayments to Providers - Recoupments and Refunds (Cornell LII copy of the Oregon Administrative Rules)
citation.excerpt: a request for a hearing or administrative review does not change the date the repayment of the Overpayment is due

rules.title: Oregon Medicaid: keep clinical records 7 years and financial records at least 5 years
rules.currentSourceStatement: Oregon Medicaid providers must keep clinical records for seven years and financial and other records for at least five years from the dates of service. This is a record-retention rule, not an overpayment look-back; the Oregon look-back is not yet verified.

citation.sourceTitle: OAR 410-120-1360 Requirements for Financial, Clinical and Other Records (Cornell LII copy of the Oregon Administrative Rules)
citation.excerpt: Retain clinical records for seven years and financial and other records described in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this rule for at least five years from the date(s) of service.

rules.title: Wisconsin Medicaid: keep records at least 5 years from payment (6 for rural health clinics)
rules.currentSourceStatement: Wisconsin Medicaid providers must retain medical, financial and other required records for at least 5 years (6 for rural health clinics), counted from the date the provider received payment. Ending participation does not end the duty to retain. This is a record-retention rule, not a recovery look-back.

citation.sourceTitle: Wis. Admin. Code DHS 106.02 General requirements for provision of services (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: shall be retained by a provider for a period of not less than 5 years, except that a rural health clinic provider shall retain the records for not less than 6 years. This period shall begin on the date on which the provider received payment from the program for the service to which the records relate.

rules.title: Oklahoma Medicaid: providers keep service records six years
rules.currentSourceStatement: Oklahoma Health Care Authority rules require providers to keep for six years the records that show the extent of services furnished to recipients, and to produce them on request. This is a record-retention rule, not an overpayment look-back; the Oklahoma look-back is not yet verified.

citation.sourceTitle: Okla. Admin. Code 317:30-3-15 Record retention (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: require that the provider retain, for a period of six years, any records necessary to disclose the extent of services

rules.title: Oklahoma Medicaid: 30 calendar days after the audit notice to repay, seek reconsideration or appeal
rules.currentSourceStatement: After an initial audit or review report, an Oklahoma Medicaid provider has 30 calendar days from the notice date to repay the overpayment, request informal reconsideration, or request a formal appeal. Claims and findings not specifically identified in an informal reconsideration request are treated as waived for a later formal appeal.

citation.sourceTitle: Okla. Admin. Code 317:30-3-2.1 Program Integrity Audits/Reviews (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: Within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of notice regarding the audit/review report, a provider may elect to: (1) Remit the identified overpayment to the OHCA; (2) Request informal reconsideration

rules.title: Louisiana Medicaid: repay lump sum within 60 days; installments no longer than two years unless approved
rules.currentSourceStatement: An arrangement to repay a Louisiana Medicaid overpayment should be a single lump-sum payment within 60 days of the arrangement being reached or imposed. Installments are allowed, but the repayment period cannot extend past two years unless the secretary or the BHSF director sets a longer period and signs the agreement.

citation.sourceTitle: La. Admin. Code tit. 50, § I-4187 Arrangement to Repay (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: should be made through a lump sum single payment within 60 days of reaching or imposing the arrangement to repay

rules.title: Washington Medicaid: make records available for six years from date of service
rules.currentSourceStatement: Washington Medicaid providers must make charts and records available to the Health Care Authority, its contractors and HHS on request for six years from the date of service, or longer where federal or state law requires. This is a record-retention rule, not a recovery look-back.

citation.sourceTitle: Wash. Admin. Code 182-502-0020 Health care record requirements (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: for six years from the date of service or longer if required specifically by federal or state law or regulation

rules.title: New York Medicaid fee-for-service: claims subject to audit for six years
rules.currentSourceStatement: For New York Medicaid fee-for-service providers, claims information is subject to audit for six years from the date the care, services or supplies were furnished or billed, whichever is later. This covers fee-for-service, not managed care plans.

citation.sourceTitle: 18 NYCRR 517.3 Audit and record retention (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: All information regarding claims for payment submitted by or on behalf of the provider is subject to audit for a period of six years from the date the care, services or supplies were furnished or billed, whichever is later

rules.title: New York Medicaid: six-year audit limit does not apply to fraud or obstruction
rules.currentSourceStatement: The six-year fee-for-service audit limit does not apply where fraud may be involved or where the provider or its agent prevents or obstructs an audit.

citation.sourceTitle: 18 NYCRR 517.3 Audit and record retention (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: This limitation does not apply to situations in which fraud may be involved or where the provider or an agent thereof prevents or obstructs an audit.

rules.title: New York Medicaid: notice of intent to audit tolls the six-year period
rules.currentSourceStatement: Once the department notifies a New York Medicaid provider of its intent to audit, the six-year retention and audit period stops running. The department may not give that notice more than six years from the date the fiscal and statistical reports were filed or required to be filed, whichever is later.

citation.sourceTitle: 18 NYCRR 517.3 Audit and record retention (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: Notification by the department to the provider of the department's intent to audit shall toll the six-year period for record retention and audit.

rules.title: New York Medicaid cost-reporting providers: fiscal reports subject to audit for six years
rules.currentSourceStatement: For New York Medicaid providers paid on reported costs, required fiscal and statistical reports are subject to audit for six years from filing or from the date they were required to be filed, whichever is later, with the same fraud and obstruction exception.

citation.sourceTitle: 18 NYCRR 517.3 Audit and record retention (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: All required fiscal and statistical reports are subject to audit for a period of six years from the date of their filing or from the date when such reports were required to be filed, whichever is later.

rules.title: MassHealth: report and return an identified overpayment within 60 days
rules.currentSourceStatement: A MassHealth provider that identifies an overpayment must report it in writing and return it within 60 days of identifying it. For payments reconciled on a cost report, the deadline is the cost report due date if that is later. The report must give the reason for the overpayment.

citation.sourceTitle: 130 CMR 450.235 Overpayments (Cornell LII copy of the MassHealth regulations)
citation.excerpt: A provider must report in writing and return any overpayments to the MassHealth agency within 60 days of the provider identifying such overpayment or, for payments subject to reconciliation based on a cost report, by the date any corresponding cost report is due, whichever is later.

rules.title: MassHealth: written reply within 30 calendar days of the overpayment notice to keep hearing rights
rules.currentSourceStatement: To keep the right to an adjudicatory hearing and judicial review, a MassHealth provider's written reply must be received within 30 calendar days of the date on the overpayment notice. The reply must address each allegation the provider disputes and may include evidence.

citation.sourceTitle: 130 CMR 450.237 Overpayments: Determination (Cornell LII copy of the MassHealth regulations)
citation.excerpt: To preserve its right to an adjudicatory hearing and judicial review, the provider must reply in writing to the MassHealth agency and such reply must be received by the MassHealth agency within 30 calendar days of the date on the overpayment notice.

rules.title: MassHealth: keep records at least six years after the date of service
rules.currentSourceStatement: MassHealth providers must keep required records at least six years after the date of service (or the date services were prescribed), or longer if generally accepted standards for their provider type require, and keep cost-report support records six years from filing. This is a record-retention rule, not an overpayment look-back.

citation.sourceTitle: 130 CMR 450.205 Recordkeeping and Disclosure (Cornell LII copy of the MassHealth regulations)
citation.excerpt: must be kept for at least six years after the date of medical services for which claims are made or the date services were prescribed, or for such length of time as may be dictated by the generally accepted standards for recordkeeping within the applicable provider type, whichever period is longer.

rules.title: Maryland Medicaid: maintain adequate records for a minimum of 6 years
rules.currentSourceStatement: Maryland Medical Assistance providers must keep adequate records for at least 6 years and make them available to the Department or its designee on request. This is a record-retention rule, not an overpayment look-back.

citation.sourceTitle: COMAR 10.09.36.03 Conditions for Participation (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: Maintain adequate records for a minimum of 6 years and make them available, upon request, to the Department or its designee

rules.title: Maryland Medicaid: refund within 60 days when both the Program and another source paid
rules.currentSourceStatement: If both the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and an insurance or other source paid for the same service, the provider must refund the Department within 60 days of receipt, in the amount of the lesser payment.

citation.sourceTitle: COMAR 10.09.36.07 Recovery and Reimbursement (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: the provider shall refund to the Department, within 60 days of receipt, the amount paid by the Program or the insurance or other source, whichever is less

rules.title: Maryland Medicaid: provider who does not reimburse owes overpayment plus audit costs; audit starts at first written notice
rules.currentSourceStatement: For audits commencing on or after July 1, 2004, a Maryland provider that fails to reimburse an overpayment owes the overpayment plus the Department's audit costs of seeking recovery. An audit is treated as commenced on the Department's initial written notice to the provider.

citation.sourceTitle: COMAR 10.09.36.07 Recovery and Reimbursement (Cornell LII copy)
citation.excerpt: the provider shall be responsible for reimbursing the Department for the amount of the overpayment and any audit costs incurred by the Department in seeking recovery of the overpayment.

rules.title: TRICARE: administrative offset may not be conducted more than 10 years after the right to collect first accrued
rules.currentSourceStatement: For TRICARE erroneous-payment debts, administrative offset under 31 U.S.C. 3716 is limited to 10 years after the right to collect first accrued, unless the facts were not known and could not reasonably have been known to the responsible TRICARE official. The limit does not apply to debts reduced to judgment. Network agreements may modify recoupment procedures; this section applies if recoupment under the network agreement is not successful.

citation.sourceTitle: 32 CFR § 199.11 Overpayments recovery (TRICARE)
citation.excerpt: administrative offset of payments under the authority of 31 U.S.C. 3716 may not be conducted more than 10 years after the Government's right to collect the debt first accrued

rules.title: TRICARE: 90 days from the initial demand letter to request an administrative review
rules.currentSourceStatement: Where no oral hearing is required, a TRICARE debtor gets an administrative review if the contractor receives a written request within 90 days of the initial demand letter. The demand letter must also state the basis and amount of the debt and the right to inspect and copy TRICARE records about it.

citation.sourceTitle: 32 CFR § 199.11 Overpayments recovery (TRICARE)
citation.excerpt: the debtor will be afforded an administrative review if the TRICARE contractor receives a written request for an administrative review within 90 days from the date of the initial demand letter

rules.title: TRICARE: interest waived on a debt paid within 30 days of the initial demand
rules.currentSourceStatement: The initial demand letter tells the debtor that interest accrues from the date of the letter and is waived on any part paid within 30 days of it. Administrative costs and penalties are charged under 31 CFR 901.

citation.sourceTitle: 32 CFR § 199.11 Overpayments recovery (TRICARE)
citation.excerpt: interest will be waived on the debt, or any portion thereof, which is paid within 30 days from the date of the initial demand notification letter

rules.title: Anthem Blue Cross (California): overpayment deducted from claim payments if no payment or direction is received
rules.currentSourceStatement: Anthem Blue Cross (California) identifies the overpayment on the EOB/RA, then sends a series of letters on a calendar-day schedule. If it has received no payment or directions it deducts the overpayment from claim payments and shows it on the EOB/RA; if that is not feasible it sends further letters and then refers the debt to collections. Read the dated sequence in SEM 8 itself, which is a plan communication, not a contract.

citation.sourceTitle: Anthem Blue Cross (California) SEM 8: Overpayment Recovery Notification Process (October 2023)
citation.locator: PDF page 1 — SEM 8, Overpayment Recovery Notification Process
citation.excerpt: If Anthem Blue Cross has not received payment or directions, the overpayment is deducted from the claims payment and is reflected on the EOB/RA.

rules.title: Anthem Blue Cross (California): overpayment timeline is counted in calendar days
rules.currentSourceStatement: The day counts in the Anthem Blue Cross (California) overpayment notification timeline are calendar days, not business days.

citation.sourceTitle: Anthem Blue Cross (California) SEM 8: Overpayment Recovery Notification Process (October 2023)
citation.locator: PDF page 1 — SEM 8, Overpayment Recovery Notification Process
citation.excerpt: Note: These are calendar days, not business days.

rules.title: Blue Shield of California: refund requested within 365 days of the original payment
rules.currentSourceStatement: When Blue Shield of California finds a payment was issued in error it will request a refund within 365 days of the original payment date, in writing, with the patient name, date of service, claim number and an explanation of the overpayment.

citation.sourceTitle: Blue Shield of California Provider Connection: Refund requests
citation.excerpt: Blue Shield will request a refund of the overpayment within 365 days of the original payment date

rules.title: Blue Shield of California: 30 working days to refund or dispute
rules.currentSourceStatement: The provider has 30 working days from receipt of the refund request to refund or give written notice that it disagrees, stating why the original payment was correct. If it does not appeal within 30 working days (or as the contract provides), Blue Shield will pursue the refund and may offset the account or assign it for recovery.

citation.sourceTitle: Blue Shield of California Provider Connection: Refund requests
citation.excerpt: Within 30 working days of receipt of the refund request, the provider must issue a refund or notify Blue Shield that they disagree with the request

rules.title: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Oklahoma: 30 days to refund before automatic retraction
rules.authority: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Oklahoma

appliesTo.payer: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Oklahoma

rules.currentSourceStatement: For lines of business converted to its new claims system, BCBSOK sends a letter requesting a refund and gives 30 days to submit it before an automatic retraction (offset). It says it contractually has the right to offset and notes the offset on the Explanation of Claims Summary. Other lines of business offset directly.

citation.sourceTitle: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Oklahoma: Right to Offset
citation.excerpt: Providers will be given 30 days to submit the refund, prior to an automatic retraction occurring
